comments:
Another simplified OOM case from a user: 
```
create table t (pk int primary key, a int, key(a));
explain select * from t where a in (1, 2, ..., 18000) and pk in (1, 2, ..., 18000);

mysql> explain select /*+ use_index(t, a) */ * from t where a in (1, 2) and pk in (1, 2);
+------------------------+---------+-----------+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| id                     | estRows | task      | access object       | operator info                                                                    |
+------------------------+---------+-----------+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| IndexReader_6          | 0.40    | root      |                     | index:IndexRangeScan_5                                                           |
| └─IndexRangeScan_5     | 0.40    | cop[tikv] | table:t, index:a(a) | range:[1 1,1 1], [1 2,1 2], [2 1,2 1], [2 2,2 2], keep order:false, stats:pseudo |
+------------------------+---------+-----------+---------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
2 rows in set (0.01 sec)
```
As you can see above, when calculating access ranges for `key(a)`, the optimizer appends `pk` after `a` implicitly, so for the condition `a in (1, 2, ..., 18000) and pk in (1, 2, ..., 18000)`, `18000*18000` access ranges will be generated, which can use a large amount of memory and even cause OOM.
We need to add some protection mechanism for range calculation.
In addition to protection,  we should reduce the memory allocation in order to avoid OOM and frequent GC which is proven significantly slow down the queries.

> In addition to protection, we should reduce the memory allocation in order to avoid OOM and frequent GC which is proven significantly slow down the queries.

Yes, totally agree. We are working on the optimization, and will keep this thread updated.
The issue is solved after PRs in #37176 are merged.
